newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts has no comment on poison scare.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts has no comment on poison scare.

text.p: Australian bakery group Arnotts Ltd said on Friday that it had no immediate comment on a reported extortion threat to plant poisoned packets of the company's biscuits (cookies) in supermarkets.

An Arnotts' spokeswoman told Reuters that Arnotts' chief executive Chris Roberts would not make any comment on the threat until he and police held a press conference at the Brisbane Police Headquarters at 9.00 a.m. Brisbane time (2300 GMT).
Arnotts is 69.91 percent owned by Campbell Soup Co.
Queensland police said late on Thursday that an extortionist had threatened to plant the poisoned biscuits unless police involved in a murder case underwent a lie detector test.

Queensland police superintendent Ron Pickering told a news conference that an extortion letter and packages containing poisoned biscuits were received by a leading food company in the states of New South Wales and Queensland on February 3. Media reports said Arnotts' biscuits were the subject of the threat.
Another Arnotts' spokesman told Reuters the company would make a statement to the stock exchange later this morning.
Police were forced to make public the extortion threat on Thursday after newspapers broke an embargo on the announcement.
"We believed from the outset that there was no threat to public safety until February 17," Pickering said.
"We had appealed to media to keep an embargo while police investigations were carried out," he said.

The extortionist demanded that New South Wales police involved in a murder investigation several years ago undergo "public polygraph tests" by February 17 or a popular brand of biscuits would be laced with poison and planted on supermarket shelves in New South Wales and Queensland.
The letter alleged that New South Wales police had set up a man for the murder of a bookmaker in 1991.
